Frosty wrote: Hi everyone, As bro Staurum pointed out, I should start understanding FTRs first before touching FLs. This will be my first homework on FTRs.

I've been reading the FTR thread and Les_Paul's journal before doing this homework. I'll post below on what I have learned from those threads. As usual, please correct any inaccurate statements Also from now on, I will do all the other homeworks here for easier reference to check my progress and any other conceptual enlightenment that all of you share to me. I also don't want to clutter this precious website with my noob level homeworks Please criticize and comment on this homework as I believe this and PAZs are the most vital concepts that RTM students should understand What I have learned on FTRs and PAZs: 1. FTRs are created on the deepest retrace after a break of important high and low, a break of FTR created in the opposite swing, a break of pre-CP, or a break of base of CP. 2. The best way to trade FTRs is to wait for an engulf of an FTR in the opposite direction and enter on a retrace to the source of the engulf, which most of the time is inside another FTR 3. There are a few types of PAZ: CP PAZ, Stacked SD PAZ, the space between 2 FTRs 4. True engulfs are those that engulfs FTRs. Some engulfs are fake engulfs to trick retail traders into taking opposite orders that the ITs want to trade against. This fake engulf (FO), usually stops at the FTR, where the ITs' orders lie 5. Engulf of an FTR, price wants to go to the next FTR in the direction of the engulf Questions that I have not yet found the answer to: 1. I don't understand why price stopped at a minor FTR instead of the blue box (I circled my question in blue oval). Any hints on this? 2. The space between the two FTRs: FTR A and B, is this the FO zone?

FTR Homework #6: Another FTR homework after spending a week off the charts to clear my mind from overloading information from RTM, As IF mentioned somewhere in FF RTM, don't try to force every information in all at once. This turned out to be a very good lesson learned I went to the second video of RTMA Lite and did more research on FTRs, LS and LS kinks. I did some deep thinking about order flow and what the retailers have been taught (outside of RTM, of course, lol).

Specifically, I really wondered why IF mentioned LS and LS Kinks to be extremely important. I want to see behind the definition and thought about the things I have been taught previously in other sites and books. What I have thought about and come up with is summed up below. I might look stupid in the process if this isn't correct, but I will definitely learn from you all and what you have to say. Please do correct this reasoning if anything or everything is all wrong as I don't want to dwell on false ideas and beliefs This explanation is for inverted LS (L-H-LL-HH-HL). For a LS (H-L-HH-LL- LH), same thing but in reverse.

Below a LS, there are trapped sellers, maybe primarily from breakout strategies (I've traded one myself called the Ross Hook). When price rises above H to make HH, these trapped sellers want to get out with as minimal loss as possible, so they sell as close to the initial L (which is the LS) to minimize losses.

This closing of sell orders from the previous break of low of LS comes in near the LS for an obvious reason, i.e. to get as close to breakeven as possible, but since every trapped sellers are doing the same thing, there are naturally some buy orders that are left unfilled. This is because to close a sell order, we need buy orders and the buy orders, in this case, is injected to the market at almost the same price are, which is the LS price level or somewhere close to it. There simply aren't many sell orders around that price area to fill all those incoming buy orders. This created the LS kink, which can be seen as a demand zone in the LTFs.

These unfilled buy orders, assuming the ITs' target, i.e. the next important FTR, hasn't been reached, we can safely assume that the ITs will pick up these unfilled buy orders and, afterwards, head for their target.

This will be the basis of my 6th FTR homework here. I put this example forward since I think this example shows what I'm trying to explain in the above paragraphs. Again, I might look stupid in the process but for the sake of my own understanding, I'll put this out here to be corrected I would really really appreciate any thoughts on this matter.
